draft.briefing: Hey, you're in Alibag! Kolaba Fort sits about 1 km out in the sea, and at low tide you can actually walk across to it. The town is known for its old marine forts, fine beaches and clean water.
draft.hungryLine: This is seafood country, so get a fish thali with pomfret or surmai, rice bhakri and a glass of pink solkadhi.

moodReplies.show-me-around: Walk out to Kolaba Fort at low tide, then head to Revdanda Fort on Revdanda beach for more history.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Kihim Beach is calm and unpolluted, a proper weekend getaway spot for Mumbaikars.
moodReplies.surprise-me: Raigad district, which Alibag heads, used to be called Colaba district.

spots.name: Kolaba Fort
spots.detail: About 1 km off the shore · A sea fort you can reach on foot at low tide

spots.name: Kihim Beach
spots.detail: Short drive · Calm coastal village with seasonal parasailing

spots.name: Revdanda Fort
spots.detail: Short drive · Historic fort right on Revdanda beach

legends.title: Home of the Konkan goddess
legends.body: Alibag is a holy place for Padmakshi Renuka. Locals know her as the goddess of Konkan.

tips.title: Check the tide first.
tips.body: You can only walk to Kolaba Fort at low tide, and not at all during the monsoon.

tips.title: Take the ferry from Mumbai.
tips.body: Mandwa Beach has direct ferry services to and from Mumbai.

story.title: Forts by the sea
story.body: Alibag grew up around its marine forts. Kolaba Fort stands in the sea off the shore, and Revdanda Fort guards Revdanda beach.

story.title: Colaba district
story.body: The district around Alibag was once called Colaba district. Today it's Raigad district, in the Konkan division of Maharashtra.

story.title: District headquarters
story.body: Alibag is the headquarters of Raigad district and a municipal council. It's part of the Mumbai Metropolitan Region, about 96 km from Mumbai.

story.title: Mumbai's weekend escape
story.body: Mumbaikars come for beaches like Kihim and Mandwa. Mandwa even has its own ferry link to the city.

food.name: Sanman restaurant
food.detail: Fish thalis with pomfret or surmai, one fried piece and one curry, plus rice bhakri and solkadhi

food.name: Fulora
food.detail: On Alibaug Rewas Rd, PNP Nagar. Seafood is the speciality, with veg and non-veg options too
